findings.title: AccentVars switch the focus outline, expand icon, filter focus border and selection fill to --primary, which the PR says it does not change.
findings.body: The PR description says the expand/collapse icon, the focus outline and the filter focus border keep the default theme's blue accent instead of `--primary`, and leaves that for a separate decision. It also says a light page has 0 changed variables. `AccentVars` sets `focusOutline`, `ExpandCollapseIcon.color`, `filterEditorFocusBorderColor`, `GroupingToolbarItem.activeBorder` and `Cell.selectedBackgroundDefault` again on the theme element. They now resolve against `--infinite-accent-color` = `var(--primary)`, so these colours change visibly in both modes. The new spec test ("uses the --primary color of the page…") checks for the new behaviour. Either remove `AccentVars` (and that test) to match the stated scope, or update the description and confirm that this visual change for existing users is intended.

findings.title: Inlining default-theme values breaks user overrides of the variables they referenced.
findings.body: `getDefaultLightValue` replaces every `var(--infinite-…)` reference with the default theme's literal value. For example, `--infinite-cell-border` becomes `1px solid #c6c6c6` and no longer reads `1px solid var(--infinite-cell-border-color)`. Before this change these values were resolved at runtime. An app that sets `--infinite-cell-border-color` or `--infinite-background` (and so on) on a shadcn grid used to change the derived border, pinned border, filter-editor border and disabled-row backgrounds. Now those are fixed in light mode. The dark vars have the same problem: they use `var(--border)` directly instead of `Cell.borderColor`. Keep the references (copy the `LightVars` values unchanged, as `AccentVars` does) and only set the leaf variables that depend on the mode. I could not see the default `LightVars` definitions, so which variables are affected is inferred.
